records.source: וַיַּעַל֩ אַבְרָ֨ם מִמִּצְרַ֜יִם ה֠וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ וְל֥וֹט עִמּ֖וֹ הַנֶּֽגְבָּה׃
records.gloss: And went up Abram from Egypt, he and his wife and all that [was] to him, and Lot with him, to the Negev.
pieces: Abram left Egypt and went up to the Negev, taking his wife and all his possessions, and Lot came too.

L.1: And Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the Negev.

R.1: Abram left Egypt and went back north to the Negev desert. His wife and Lot went with him, and he took everything he owned.

decisions.choice: went up: traveled north and uphill
decisions.reason: Going from Egypt to Canaan is always "going up", as going to Egypt is "going down" (12:10): the land rises toward the hill country.

records.heading: Abram and Lot part ways

records.source: וְאַבְרָ֖ם כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד בַּמִּקְנֶ֕ה בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וּבַזָּהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And Abram [was] heavy very in livestock, in silver and in gold.
pieces: By now Abram was a very rich man, with herds and flocks, silver and gold.

L.2: And Abram [was] very rich in livestock, in silver and in gold.

R.2: Abram was very rich. He had many animals and a lot of silver and gold.

decisions.choice: heavy: rich
decisions.reason: The word means heavy, and so rich or weighty. It is the root of "glory" (kavod). Abram's wealth comes partly from Egypt (12:16) and sets up the quarrel that follows.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְמַסָּעָ֔יו מִנֶּ֖גֶב וְעַד־בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל עַד־הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר־הָ֨יָה שָׁ֤ם אָֽהֳלוֹ֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה בֵּ֥ין בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל וּבֵ֥ין הָעָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he went by his stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where had been his tent at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
pieces: From the Negev he traveled in stages back to Bethel, to the spot between Bethel and Ai where he had first pitched his tent,

L.3: And he went on by stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,

R.3: From the Negev he moved from place to place until he came back to the place between Bethel and Ai where he had first put up his tent.

decisions.choice: at the beginning: back where he started
decisions.reason: Abram returns to the place where he first camped and built an altar (12:8). After the failure in Egypt he goes back to the place of worship.

records.source: אֶל־מְקוֹם֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥שָׂה שָׁ֖ם בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א שָׁ֛ם אַבְרָ֖ם בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: to [the] place of the altar which he had made there at the first; and called there Abram on [the] name of YHWH.
pieces: where he had built the altar before. There Abram called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: to the place of the altar that he had made there at first; and there Abram called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: This was where he had built an altar. There Abram prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} again.

records.source: וְגַם־לְל֔וֹט הַהֹלֵ֖ךְ אֶת־אַבְרָ֑ם הָיָ֥ה צֹאן־וּבָקָ֖ר וְאֹהָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And also to Lot, who went with Abram, belonged sheep and cattle and tents.
pieces: Lot, traveling with Abram, had his own flocks and herds and tents as well.

L.5: And Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks and herds and tents.

R.5: Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had sheep, cattle and tents.

decisions.choice: tents: households
decisions.reason: "Tents" stands for the households living in them, servants and herdsmen included.

records.source: וְלֹא־נָשָׂ֥א אֹתָ֛ם הָאָ֖רֶץ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת יַחְדָּ֑ו כִּֽי־הָיָ֤ה רְכוּשָׁם֙ רָ֔ב וְלֹ֥א יָֽכְל֖וּ לָשֶׁ֥בֶת יַחְדָּֽו׃
records.gloss: And not supported them the land to dwell together, for was their possessions much, and not they were able to dwell together.
pieces: The land could not sustain both of them living side by side; they had so much that they could not stay together.

L.6: And the land could not support them dwelling together, for their possessions were so great that they could not dwell together.

R.6: There was not enough grass and water for both of them to live in the same place, because they had too many animals.

decisions.choice: the land could not support them: not enough pasture and water
decisions.reason: Herds need grazing land and wells. Two large households in one area compete for both. The blessing of wealth itself brings strain.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי־רִ֗יב בֵּ֚ין רֹעֵ֣י מִקְנֵֽה־אַבְרָ֔ם וּבֵ֖ין רֹעֵ֣י מִקְנֵה־ל֑וֹט וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י אָ֖ז יֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And was strife between [the] herdsmen of [the] livestock of Abram and between [the] herdsmen of [the] livestock of Lot; and the Canaanite[s] and the Perizzite[s] then dwelt in the land.
pieces: Before long Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen were at odds with each other. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also settled in the land.

L.7: And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram's livestock and the herdsmen of Lot's livestock. And the Canaanites and the Perizzites were then living in the land.

R.7: The men who looked after Abram's animals began to quarrel with the men who looked after Lot's animals. The Canaanites and the Perizzites also lived in the land then.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites and Perizzites were living in the land: little room, and watching neighbors
decisions.reason: The note explains why there was so little room, and it may hint that the quarrel was a poor witness before the people of the land. The Perizzites may have been village dwellers of the hill country.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַבְרָ֜ם אֶל־ל֗וֹט אַל־נָ֨א תְהִ֤י מְרִיבָה֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔יךָ וּבֵ֥ין רֹעַ֖י וּבֵ֣ין רֹעֶ֑יךָ כִּֽי־אֲנָשִׁ֥ים אַחִ֖ים אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Abram to Lot, let there not be, please, strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for men brothers we [are].
pieces: So Abram said to Lot, "There should be no quarrel between us, or between your herdsmen and mine. We are family.

L.8: And Abram said to Lot, "Please let there be no strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we [are] kinsmen.

R.8: So Abram said to Lot, "We should not quarrel, and our men should not quarrel either. We are family.

decisions.choice: we are brothers: we are close kin
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is used of any close relatives; Lot is Abram's nephew (11:27). Abram, the elder, takes the first step toward peace.

records.source: הֲלֹ֤א כָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ הִפָּ֥רֶד נָ֖א מֵעָלָ֑י אִם־הַשְּׂמֹ֣אל וְאֵימִ֔נָה וְאִם־הַיָּמִ֖ין וְאַשְׂמְאִֽילָה׃
records.gloss: Is not all the land before you? Separate, please, from me; if the left, then I will go right, and if the right, then I will go left.
pieces: The whole land is open to you. Let us go our separate ways. You take the left and I will take the right, or you take the right and I will take the left."

L.9: Is not the whole land before you? Please separate from me. If [you take] the left, then I will go to the right; or if the right, then I will go to the left."

R.9: Look at all the land in front of you. Let us go different ways. You choose first. If you go one way, I will go the other way."

decisions.choice: if the left, I will go right: Abram gives Lot the first choice
decisions.reason: As the elder and the one to whom the land was promised (12:7), Abram had the right to choose. He gives it up, trusting God's promise. "Left" and "right" can also mean north and south, as a person faces east.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂא־ל֣וֹט אֶת־עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־כָּל־כִּכַּ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן כִּ֥י כֻלָּ֖הּ מַשְׁקֶ֑ה לִפְנֵ֣י׀שַׁחֵ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־סְדֹם֙ וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֔ה כְּגַן־יְהוָה֙ כְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בֹּאֲכָ֖ה צֹֽעַר׃
records.gloss: And lifted Lot his eyes and saw all [the] plain of the Jordan, that all of it [was] well-watered, before YHWH destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like [the] garden of YHWH, like [the] land of Egypt, as you go to Zoar.
pieces: Lot looked out over the Jordan plain and saw water everywhere, all the way to Zoar, as in the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or the land of Egypt. (That was before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)

L.10: And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw all the plain of the Jordan, that it was all well watered, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like the land of Egypt, in the direction of Zoar.

R.10: Lot looked around and saw that the whole Jordan valley, as far as Zoar, had plenty of water. It was like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or like the land of Egypt. (This was before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah.)

decisions.choice: the plain of the Jordan: the circle of land around the lower Jordan
decisions.reason: The word means a circle or round area: the valley of the Jordan near the Dead Sea, then fertile and well watered.

decisions.choice: like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt: attractive, and dangerous
decisions.reason: The plain looks like Eden and like Egypt, both places of plenty. But the note "before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah" warns the reader what lies ahead (chapter 19).

decisions.choice: the note about Sodom in brackets at the end
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move the narrator's aside to the end of the sentence and set it in brackets, so the description reads clearly.

records.source: וַיִּבְחַר־ל֣וֹ ל֗וֹט אֵ֚ת כָּל־כִּכַּ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיִּסַּ֥ע ל֖וֹט מִקֶּ֑דֶם וַיִּפָּ֣רְד֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ מֵעַ֥ל אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And chose for himself Lot all [the] plain of the Jordan, and set out Lot eastward, and they separated each from his brother.
pieces: So Lot chose the whole Jordan plain for himself and moved off to the east. The two of them parted.

L.11: And Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan, and Lot set out eastward; and they separated from each other.

R.11: So Lot chose the Jordan valley for himself and moved east. That is how Abram and Lot separated.

decisions.choice: eastward: moving east again
decisions.reason: In Genesis, going east has marked moving away from God's presence (3:24; 4:16; 11:2). Lot chooses by what his eyes see.

records.source: אַבְרָ֖ם יָשַׁ֣ב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־כְּנָ֑עַן וְל֗וֹט יָשַׁב֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַכִּכָּ֔ר וַיֶּאֱהַ֖ל עַד־סְדֹֽם׃
records.gloss: Abram dwelt in [the] land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt in [the] cities of the plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
pieces: Abram remained in Canaan; Lot settled among the towns of the plain and moved his camp as far as Sodom.

L.12: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot settled among the cities of the plain and pitched his tent as far as Sodom.

R.12: Abram stayed in Canaan. Lot lived among the towns in the valley and moved his tents close to Sodom.

decisions.choice: as far as Sodom: drawing near to danger
decisions.reason: Lot moves his tent step by step toward Sodom; by 14:12 he lives in it, and by 19:1 he sits in its gate.

records.source: וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י סְדֹ֔ם רָעִ֖ים וְחַטָּאִ֑ים לַיהוָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And the men of Sodom [were] evil and sinners against YHWH exceedingly.
pieces: The people of Sodom, however, were evil and grievous sinners against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: Now the men of Sodom were wicked, great sinners against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: The people of Sodom were very wicked. They sinned terribly against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: wicked, great sinners against the LORD: the warning sounded
decisions.reason: The narrator's comment explains the destruction to come (18:20; 19:4-13). Ezekiel 16:49-50 describes Sodom's sins as pride, excess and neglect of the poor, together with detestable acts.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The word can refer to the inhabitants generally; Balanced and Readable say "people", Literal keeps "men".

records.source: וַֽיהוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם אַחֲרֵי֙ הִפָּֽרֶד־ל֣וֹט מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִן־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה שָׁ֑ם צָפֹ֥נָה וָנֶ֖גְבָּה וָקֵ֥דְמָה וָיָֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And YHWH said to Abram after had separated Lot from him, lift up, please, your eyes and see from the place where you [are], northward and southward and eastward and westward,
pieces: After Lot had gone, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Raise your eyes and look out from where you stand, to the north and south, east and west.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, "Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,

R.14: After Lot left, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Look around you in every direction: north, south, east and west.

decisions.choice: lift up your eyes: God shows Abram what Lot saw for himself
decisions.reason: Lot "lifted up his eyes" and chose for himself (verse 10). Now God tells Abram to lift up his eyes, and gives him everything he sees.

records.source: כִּ֧י אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְךָ֣ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֖ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: For all the land that you are seeing, to you I will give it, and to your offspring forever.
pieces: I am giving you all the land you can see, to you and your descendants for all time.

L.15: for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.

R.15: I will give all the land you can see to you and to your family after you, forever.

decisions.choice: forever: for all time to come
decisions.reason: The word (olam) means a very long or unlimited time. The promise is lasting.

records.source: וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֖ כַּעֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀אִם־יוּכַ֣ל אִ֗ישׁ לִמְנוֹת֙ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ גַּֽם־זַרְעֲךָ֖ יִמָּנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will make your offspring like [the] dust of the earth, so that if one is able to count the dust of the earth, also your offspring could be counted.
pieces: I will make your descendants as countless as the dust of the earth; only if someone could count the dust could your descendants be counted.

L.16: And I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone could count the dust of the earth, your offspring also could be counted.

R.16: I will give you so many descendants that they will be like the dust of the earth. No one can count the dust, and no one will be able to count your descendants.

decisions.choice: like the dust of the earth: beyond counting
decisions.reason: Later God compares Abram's descendants to the stars (15:5) and the sand (22:17): pictures of numbers beyond counting, made to a man with no child.

records.source: ק֚וּם הִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בָּאָ֔רֶץ לְאָרְכָּ֖הּ וּלְרָחְבָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י לְךָ֖ אֶתְּנֶֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: Arise, walk about in the land, through its length and its breadth, for to you I will give it.
pieces: Go and travel the land from end to end and side to side, because I am giving it to you."

L.17: Arise, walk through the land, its length and its breadth, for I will give it to you."

R.17: Go and walk through the whole land, from one end to the other, because I am giving it to you."

decisions.choice: walk through the land: as an owner surveys his property
decisions.reason: Walking through a land could be a way of taking possession of it (Joshua 1:3). Abram is to explore what will be his.

records.source: וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ל אַבְרָ֗ם וַיָּבֹ֛א וַיֵּ֛שֶׁב בְּאֵלֹנֵ֥י מַמְרֵ֖א אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וַיִּֽבֶן־שָׁ֥ם מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And moved his tent Abram and came and dwelt at [the] great trees of Mamre, which [are] at Hebron, and he built there an altar to YHWH.
pieces: So Abram moved his tents and went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.18: And Abram moved his tent and came and settled by the great trees of Mamre, which are at Hebron, and he built there an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: So Abram moved his tents and went to live by the big trees of Mamre, near the town of Hebron. There he built an altar to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the great trees of Mamre at Hebron: Abram's home in the hill country
decisions.reason: Mamre, near Hebron in the southern hill country, becomes Abraham's main home (14:13; 18:1). Sarah and Abraham are buried nearby (23:19; 25:9).
